title: Three clocks converted ad hoc: one playout clock owns 'when is it heard'
acceptance: PlayoutClock over a fake context {currentTime 12.05, outputLatency 0.1}: heardNow() -> 11.95 (context time minus the output latency); with outputLatency absent/undefined -> 12.05 (today's value, no regression)

body:
## Summary
The stage converts between three clocks: the AudioContext's, the speakers', and the wall. It does this in four places, by hand, and none of them knows the audio's output latency. The face reads the mouth at the context's time (player.ts:198), the captions get the context's time raw (useVoice.ts:118, :158), and the `played` report rebuilds wall time from whichever frame tick noticed the start (session.ts:66). Add one `PlayoutClock` module that owns the answer to "when is the sample at context time t heard, on the audio clock and on the wall". It samples `getOutputTimestamp()` and `outputLatency` once per tick. The face, the captions and the reports all read from it.

## Description
This leans on voice-io `speech-timing-timeline` (the consumer maps samples through its own schedule and adds its output latency) and talking-avatar `viseme-drive` (look up the shape at the playback position plus the device's output latency; the renderer owns the lead). It is also the `one-authority-per-vocabulary` law applied to time.

Today's context is created with `latencyHint: 'playback'` (webaudio.ts:19), the largest-buffer hint. The mouth is then driven ahead of the context time by 35 ms, and so ahead of the sound by 35 ms plus the whole output path. The product's own detectability bound is 45 ms early (watch.rs:46-48), and no check measures face against sound. The recorder measures speech about 200 ms after `played`, of which only about 70 ms is the Kokoro leading silence (recording.md:198-200). The `played` time is also sampled non-atomically: wall() and currentTime are read on a rAF tick, so a quantized context clock leaks tick jitter into the times that `av_sync`, the clip cutter and `voiced` read.

`PlayoutClock` takes an `AudioLike` and gains two optional members: `outputLatency` and `outputTimestamp()`. It exposes `heardNow()` (context seconds, monotone), `heardAt(ctxStart)` (the context time the start is heard) and `wallOf(ctxTime)` (epoch ms, from the coherent contextTime/performanceTime pair). The player's `signalAt` and `tell` read heard time and keep `VISEME_LEAD_MS` as the renderer's own lead. The session's `started` hook reports `wallOf(heardAt(p.start))`, which matches the contract's own words, 'the part's audio started playing' (contract.md:1207). `useVoice` hands captions `heardNow()`. Where the browser reports nothing, the latency is 0 and the result is today's behaviour. Gate: architecture. The *constant* in `av_offset_ms` shrinks by the latency the browser reports, so recording.md's ~200 ms note is updated. `av_sync` judges spread and drift, not the constant (watch.rs:369), and the clip cut still opens before `played`.

## Flow
- playout.test.ts first: heardNow, wallOf, monotone clamp, absent-latency fallback (red)
- playout.ts, plus the AudioLike optional members in player.ts and the real ones in webaudio.ts (green)
- player.test.ts: resting before the heard start, and the viseme at 0 ms at heard start minus the lead (red), then player.ts reads the clock
- report.test.ts: at_wall_ms includes the latency and is tick-independent (red), then session.ts uses clock.wallOf
- useVoice.ts: the caption and unvoiced stamps use heardNow
- DESIGN.md (also fixes its stale 'Past 6 s', since MAX_AHEAD_S is 16 at player.ts:28) and recording.md's offset note

## Expected impact
The mouth, the captions and the reported play time all describe the moment the sound is heard, in one place. A new consumer, such as a gesture or a lower-third keyed to a word, gets the right time by construction instead of a fifth hand conversion. Tick jitter leaves the `played` times that the watched checks and the clips read.

## Evaluation
Claim: one playout clock makes face, captions and played reports agree on heard time, latency-corrected and tick-independent
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no clock module; player/session ignore latency; at_wall_ms depends on the observing tick)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first against fake AudioLike with outputLatency/outputTimestamp
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: player.ts:198 `const ms = (now - e.start) * 1000 + VISEME_LEAD_MS;` | player.ts:291 `const s = this.signalAt(this.audio.currentTime);` | player.ts:229 `this.events.started?.(part(e), now - e.start);` | session.ts:66 `this.report(playedFrame(p.runId, p.seq, p.part, this.wall() - lateS * 1000));` | useVoice.ts:118 `const now = () => audio.audio.currentTime;` | useVoice.ts:158 `captions.view(run, said, audio.audio.currentTime, streamNow)` | webaudio.ts:19 `new AudioContext({ latencyHint: "playback" })` | `git grep -n "outputLatency\|baseLatency\|getOutputTimestamp" -- apps packages crates tools docs` -> no output | recording.md:198-200 'speech starts about 200 ms after its `played` time ... about 70 ms of that is the silence at the start of each Kokoro sentence' | watch.rs:46-48 AV_SYNC_EARLY_MS = 45

critic.reason: Strong move; one acceptance case encodes a latency double-count.

revision: Rewrite case 3: with outputTimestamp {contextTime 11.9, performanceTime p}, wall(timeOrigin+p)=1_000_000 and outputLatency 0.1, at_wall_ms = 1_000_100 (start minus contextTime; latency NOT added again because the output timestamp already includes it), and set the fake's tick wall()/currentTime so today's wall()-lateS*1000 yields a different value.

title: 'Voice ready' while lines vanish: a voice panel that shows the loss and acts
acceptance: session receives skipped frames reason late x1 and queue_full x2 for the followed run -> health().skipped == {late:1, queue_full:2, error:0}, and the panel row reads '3 lines not voiced by the daemon (2 queue full, 1 late)'

a non-JSON frame then an utterance with a bad sample_rate -> health().badFrames == 2 and health().lastBad == 'voice utterance frame: bad sample_rate' (useVoice wires onBadFrame; today nothing listens)
the player's cap drops one line -> health().stageDropped == 1 and health().behindS equals player.ahead (rounded to 0.1 s); a run change resets all counts to 0
the socket closes twice -> health().reconnect == {attempt:2, nextInMs:2000}; retryNow() opens a new socket at once and clears the pending timer; a further close resumes backoff from attempt 3

broadcast view (?broadcast=1) -> no panel and no action rendered; the status rule for broadcast is unchanged
premise: apps/stage/src/voice/session.ts:37,144 - onBadFrame exists, but useVoice.ts:119-129 never passes it: bad frames are dropped with no trace (git grep onBadFrame -> only session.ts and session.test.ts:56)
apps/stage/src/voice/session.ts:161-163 - a skipped frame's reason (late|queue_full|error, parsed at frame.ts:79) is thrown away; only (run_id, seq) reaches the captions
apps/stage/src/voice/player.ts:110-113,121-125 - dropped, droppedLines and ahead are kept 'for tests and the debug surface' (player.ts:133); git grep shows no consumer outside player.ts and its tests
apps/stage/src/Controls.tsx:183-186 - the operator sees one label plus a reason string: 'voice ready' stays up while the stage drops lines and the daemon skips them

apps/stage/src/voice/useVoice.ts:85-89 - a suspended context in the operator view reads 'audio is blocked until a click on the page', but the only unlockAudio() call outside broadcast is App.tsx:208, inside toggleVoice(on) - clicking the page does nothing; the operator must toggle the voice off and on
apps/stage/src/voice/session.ts:167-173 - a closed socket shows 'reconnecting' with backoff up to 10 s and no way to retry now and no attempt count
rollback: One feature commit plus its tests: health.ts is additive, session/useVoice gain a health() snapshot and retryNow(), and Controls renders a panel. Reverting the commit restores the single label; no contract, socket frame or storage change.

body:
## Summary
The operator view tells the stage's operator one word about the voice: off, starting, ready or degraded. The stage and the daemon know much more. They know how many seconds of audio wait behind the playhead, which lines the stage's cap dropped, which lines the daemon skipped and why (late, queue full, error), which frames failed the guard, and which reconnect attempt is pending. All of that is thrown away or kept only for tests. The operator decides blind whether the voice is keeping up, and the one action the status asks for ('click on the page') does nothing. This card makes the voice chip open a small panel that shows those facts for the followed run and offers the two actions they call for: Enable audio, and Reconnect now.

## Description
This leans on voice-io `voice-ux-integration` ('an enabled-looking voice button does nothing' is its named failure, and the 'ready'-but-blocked state is exactly that). It also leans on the golden path's rule that everything spoken must exist as text, so a line that was not voiced must be visible as such to the operator, with its reason. `health.ts` is a pure reducer over the events the session already sees: skipped by reason, stage_dropped, a bad frame with its message, a reconnect scheduled/opened, and a run change that resets the counts. `VoiceSession.health()` returns its snapshot plus `player.ahead`. `retryNow()` clears the backoff timer and opens. `shownStatus` gains an `action: 'unlock'|'retry'|null`, so the chip renders a button instead of prose. The unlock button calls `unlockAudio()` inside its own click without flipping the toggle. The broadcast view renders nothing new. The counts are per followed run, which matches what the daemon logs to voice.jsonl, so the panel and the `voiced` check describe the same lines.

## Flow
- health.test.ts and session.test.ts cases first (red)
- health.ts reducer; session.ts feeds it from the skipped, utterance, bad-frame, close and open paths, and gains retryNow()
- useVoice wires onBadFrame, exposes health on a throttled re-render (App already repaints every 32 ms live, App.tsx:170-175) and the action on the status
- Controls.tsx: the chip becomes a button that opens the panel (behind N s, cap-dropped N, daemon-skipped N by reason, bad frames N + last message, reconnect attempt and countdown) with Enable audio and Reconnect now; names.ts holds the labels; styles.css
- DESIGN.md's voice section

## Expected impact
Unlocking audio after a reload takes 1 click instead of 2 (toggle off, toggle on), and the instruction is no longer false. A voice that silently loses lines, whether to the daemon's queue, lateness or the stage's cap, shows that loss while it happens instead of only in a post-run `voiced` check. A dead socket can be retried at once instead of waiting up to 10 s of backoff.

## Evaluation
Claim: the operator sees why lines go unvoiced and can act on blocked audio and a dead socket from the chip
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no health snapshot, onBadFrame unwired, reasons discarded, no retryNow, no unlock action)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (vitest on fake socket/audio, shownStatus unit)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: session.ts:161-163 `} else if (this.runId === null || v.run_id === this.runId) { // a skipped line ... this.o.onSkipped?.(v.run_id, v.seq);` (reason dropped) | useVoice.ts:119-129 VoiceSession options have no onBadFrame | `git grep -n "\.ahead\b\|droppedLines\|onBadFrame" -- apps/stage/src` -> only player.ts, session.ts, and *.test.ts | useVoice.ts:88 `return { state: "degraded", reason: "audio is blocked until a click on the page" };` | App.tsx:206-208 `(on: boolean) => { if (on) unlockAudio();` is the only non-broadcast unlock (git grep unlockAudio) | Controls.tsx:183-186 single label + reason span | session.ts:172 backoff `Math.min(10_000, 500 * 2 ** Math.min(this.retry, 5))`

critic.reason: Grounded, testable, fixes a false operator instruction.
